title: Spengler wins Norisring Race 2 after the Audis collide
dek: Bruno Spengler took the lead on lap one and won DTM Race 2 at the Norisring for BMW by 5.765 seconds from Jamie Green, after Nico Müller spun pole-sitter René Rast.

chapters.title: Rast leads after a wild Saturday
text: Saturday had gone to René Rast. He stalled at the start of Race 1, was last before the first corner and still won by 34.498 seconds after stopping on lap three just before the safety car. Nico Müller finished second after passing Joel Eriksson at the last corner, giving Audi a one-two. Rast left Saturday with 118 points as championship leader, with Müller second and Philipp Eng of BMW third on 91, 27 points behind.
Sunday's race followed a morning qualifying session, and the track was much cooler than on Saturday, at around 31 degrees.

chapters.title: Rast snatches pole with 30 seconds left
text: Most drivers had only set banker laps when the session was red-flagged after five minutes because Timo Glock's BMW stopped exiting the chicane. After a five-minute delay, the field split: some went straight out, others stayed in the garage. Müller was one of the first back on track and immediately beat Loïc Duval's early benchmark with a 46.264s.

Jamie Green came within 0.060s of that before improving to 46.153s, which Müller matched, and it looked good enough for pole until Rast went 46.146s with 30 seconds left. That put Audis in the first four places, with Duval on 46.186s. Eng was the leading BMW, 0.046s off pole, and Mike Rockenfeller was sixth. Glock, who had not set a representative time before stopping, was last on 51.883s.

Penalties then reshaped the order. Green, Rockenfeller and Dennis were each moved back five places, which left Rast on pole from Müller, Duval, Eng and Bruno Spengler, with Sheldon van der Linde sixth and Green seventh. Rockenfeller started 11th, Daniel Juncadella 13th as the best of the Aston Martins, Glock 17th and Jake Dennis 18th.

chapters.title: Three Audis go wide and Spengler takes the lead
text: Rast made a better start than a day earlier but was outflanked by Müller and Duval on the run to the first corner. All three Audis then ran deeper than necessary into the hairpin, and Spengler, who had started fifth after a lightning getaway, went through into the lead ahead of Müller.

At the chicane Rast went around the outside of Müller and appeared to have the place, only for Müller to hit him in the second part of the corner and leave him facing the wrong way. Müller was given a drive-through penalty for the contact. Rast and Duval both pitted at the end of the first lap, and Rast spent the rest of the race fighting back from the rear.

chapters.title: Green cuts the gap, Spengler breaks clear
text: Free of Müller, Spengler settled into a comfortable lead. Green, who had been running fourth, pitted at the end of lap 16, and during the stop phase he cleared Eng and Robin Frijns to move into second. Spengler stopped at the end of lap 32 of 70 and rejoined with fresh tyres, which left Green within a second of him for a handful of laps.

The threat did not last. Spengler pulled away from the Audi and built a buffer of about five seconds for the final stages. Behind them Frijns held third thanks to passes on Duval and Eng, while Rockenfeller, who had started 11th and made no attempt to save his tyres, worked his way up to fourth.

chapters.title: Rockenfeller takes the last podium place
text: Spengler crossed the line after 70 laps in 56:15.610, 5.765 seconds clear of Green. Rockenfeller caught Frijns with about 15 minutes to run, and the two Audis ran three laps separated by four tenths before Rockenfeller got a better run out of the chicane ten laps from home and took the inside line at the second hairpin to claim the last podium place. He then chased Green, finishing 1.068 seconds behind him in third, with Frijns fourth.

Eng finished fifth, 16.365 seconds behind the winner, having been on course for sixth until Marco Wittmann slowed in the closing laps, and Wittmann was classified 16th, six laps down. Duval was sixth after his lap-one stop, with Rast seventh and Müller eighth, 25.480 and 29.080 seconds behind. Glock climbed from 17th to ninth, and Juncadella took the last point in tenth. Sheldon van der Linde and Paul di Resta did not finish. Müller set the fastest lap of the race, 46.618s on lap eight.

chapters.title: Spengler becomes the Norisring's sole record winner
text: The win was Spengler's 16th in the DTM and his fifth at the Norisring, which made him the sole record winner at the circuit; Green, on four, had been level with him. It ended a two-year DTM win drought, his last victory having come at the Norisring in 2017. “I'm delighted with my record win at the Norisring,” he said, and praised the way the tyres coped with the heavy loads of the street circuit.

Audi still took six of the top eight places. Green, second, said he had been able to push his tyres for 54 laps, which he saw as the key to the result, while Rockenfeller said he had had no tyre-management plan on his way from 11th on the grid to the podium. Rast limited the damage by recovering to seventh after his spin, and Müller, who served his drive-through, finished eighth. Eng had run on podium pace at times but could not stay with the fastest cars on his second set of tyres.

Rast left Nuremberg still leading the championship, now on 127 points, with Müller on 102 and Eng on 101. Spengler's win lifted him to fourth. Eng was 26 points behind Rast and a single point behind Müller.

R-Motorsport had a better day. Juncadella scored in both races, finishing tenth on Sunday after a poor start, in what was his best weekend of the season. Habsburg missed a point by one place in 11th. Wittmann's home weekend ended with a 16th place after he slowed late in the race. The DTM now heads to the TT Circuit Assen for the fifth round on 20–21 July.

facts.v: Spengler's fifth win at the Norisring made him the only driver with that many victories at the circuit, one more than Green.
